newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASJ to take "unfair" market share says chairman.
newsitem.headline: ASJ to take "unfair" market share says chairman.

text.p: Capturing an unfair share of the resistor market lies at the heart of the expansion plans of soon-to-be listed Singapore electronics firm ASJ Holdings Ltd (ASJ), its chairman told Reuters on Friday.
"Our aim is to go out and capture an unfair share of the market," ASJ chairman Fong Yow Wai said in an interview after launching an initial public offer for shares in the company.

Fong said Singapore imports more than Singapore $300 million (US$214 million) worth of resistors a year, "so it gives us a good position to capture an unfair share of this market because we are on the doorstep".
"We invested substantially in 1994 and 1995 and we are now reaping the benefits from that," Fong said.

ASJ makes and markets electronic and non-electronic components through three subsidiaries. It grew at a compound annual rate of 41 percent between 1991 and 1995 to reach turnover of S$34.01 million, and estimates it will grow a further 10.3 percent to S$37.5 million in 1996.

Profits have shown a stronger surge, up 172 percent over the period and predicted to leap 66.5 percent in 1996 to S$4.48 million from S$2.69 million previously. Fong said he was confident ASJ would maintain "very stable growth".
ASJ expects to raise S$7.2 million from the placing of 15 million shares on the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
About S$3.5 million of the proceeds will be invested in new machinery, process automation and research and development at its Singapore plant.
Another S$1.5 million will be spent on creating warehouse and distribution facilities in Malaysia and Thailand. The balance will pay-off bank borrowings and add to working capital.

Already, S$6 million has been invested in ASJ's Singapore plant, giving an estimated output of four billion units in 1996, roughly two percent of the estimated 220 billion-unit global resistor market and twice the 1.9 billion units it made in 1995.
As the market is expected to reach 265 billion units by 1999, Fong said prospects for the sector and ASJ looked good.
He said ASJ would follow its customers as they expanded into new markets and new geographical regions.
"Our strategy is to diversify our customer base, to invest in technology, in warehousing in Thailand and Malaysia and to expand in Europe, the U.S. and Asia," Fong said.
He said expansion could come from entering niche product areas as well as linking up with multinational manufacturers operating in Singapore to become their global resistor supplier.

Fong said a relationship with major Taiwanese resistor maker Yageo gave ASJ extra raw materials purchasing power as well as access to developing technology and manufacturing proceedures. ($1 = S$1.40)
